comments.author: InterstellarReddit
comments.body:
So ummm steam?

You can list open source games on Steam, and there’s even lists and communities that track it.

What are you adding that’s different that people should start listing on your platform versus Steam, which dominates the PC market?

replies.author: i_rate_slop
replies.body:
There’s nothing wrong with having a site dedicated to open source games. Nothing is stopping anybody from *also* putting them on Steam. If people want to use it, let them.

The bigger question is: will this become a malware distribution channel in -10 seconds?

replies.author: RisaPulseance
replies.body:
Github also doesn't scan for malware, and pretty much for now all games link to github.

It's possible though to work on launcher - it's more control.

replies.author: Southern_Sun_2106
replies.body: Hey, I bookmarked! Thank you for putting this together. It definitely meets a need, wishing you the best of luck!

replies.author: i_rate_slop
replies.body:
Ok? 

1. There’s tons of malware on GitHub  
2. Launcher doesn’t change anything  
3. Gamers aren’t developers. They’re going to trust the platform like Steam. Steam puts a lot of effort into reducing malware on their platform.

It’s still a cool project. I wouldn’t install anything from it that isn’t reputable.

replies.author: Southern_Sun_2106
replies.body:
I like GitHub links here; good luck finding open-source games on steam. There is a clear advantage to having a purely open-source focus.

The better question is, what is he \*\*removing\*\* here from what steam has - a bunch of corrupt money-bags that obviously support the "you will have nothing and will be happy!" world that has also stagnated steam into a boring platform that it is today.

comments.body:
